_comment: Entries for /ai, rendered by scripts/build-ai.mjs. An entry earns its place by an outcome someone else can check: a change merged into a repository Ben does not own, a competition result, a published audit, a released tool. Work in progress does not qualify, and neither does a result that exists only in Ben's own notes. Entries describe what happened and never which model, agent or tool did it; scripts/check-ai-wins.mjs fails the build on a name in the title or summary, while `where` and link labels carry the venue's own name. Links are optional because some venues publish no permanent page, but a link that is present must be absolute https. Newest first is produced by the builder, so order here does not matter. `quotes` are third parties' words, copied verbatim from a public page (Ben, 2026-09-15): they may name whatever the author named, so the name check does not apply to them, and every quote must link to the page it was copied from.

wins.title: Prompt-cache hit rate on the statusline, merged into a menu-bar usage tracker
wins.summary: The cache hit ratio was visible only in a cost report after the fact. A new statusline component shows it as a colored percentage and, for ten minutes after a miss, the cause in one word: a changed system prompt, a changed tool set, a model switch, rewritten history, an expired TTL or the server. A cache reset shows up when it happens instead of later as a slow, expensive session.

wins.title: Packomania: 318 records in two tables
wins.where: Eckard Specht's Packomania tables of equal spheres in a cube and in a 4-dimensional ball
wins.summary: Packings of N equal spheres with a larger radius than the table listed, each checked in exact arithmetic: 239 in a unit cube (N from 135 to 981) and 79 in a 4-dimensional ball (N from 65 to 300). Every file beats the table's radius for N and for every larger N, a local polish of the posted packing, and the best radius in the Moki & Julio collection, each by at least 1e-7. Gains run from 1.1e-7 to 4.7e-4 in the cube and from 1.3e-7 to 3.6e-4 in the ball. Eckard Specht (Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg) put the cube packings in the table on 2026-11-08 and the 4-D ones on 2026-11-09, citing the packing-records data set.

wins.title: V3R1T4S: a better spherical code for 64 points in 31 dimensions
wins.summary: 64 unit vectors in R^31 whose largest pairwise cosine is 0.0303197333750, below the 0.030322662292 that spherical-codes.org lists for (31, 64) by 2.93e-6, on a row not marked optimal. The package carries the vectors, a checker written from the definition and the table snapshot. The maintainers confirmed the value with their own exact checker, found that the code differs from the posted one, and merged it on 2026-11-07.

wins.title: Lagrange Bend hidden objects: DDUST #361 won by room 237
wins.where: Lagrange Bend by jiwa, Art Blocks Studio, Ethereum
wins.summary: Lagrange Bend has 400 rooms and hid seven objects in them. An object goes to the room whose ghost dies at a hidden death count: the 20-death range is published, the count is not. Room 237 won the sixth object, DDUST #361 by jiwa, inside the 1180-1199 range on 2026-11-07. Ben's three rooms were played by a program that ran every visit through a simulation before sending it. Other rooms won the first five. The award, the claim and the transfer to thebenmeadows.eth are Ethereum transactions.

wins.title: Three audits of a platform's claimed fixes, posted on its own issues
wins.summary: Each one checked a claim on the platform's issue tracker against the code or the running service: a merged gateway whose endpoint was not answering (2026-06-19), a fix reported complete with one of its three gaps still open (2026-07-08), and a guard where two of the three stated reasons did not hold in the code (2026-08-04). Each verdict carries its evidence on the issue.

wins.title: Grassmannian packings table: 1,442 records improved
wins.where: Henry Cohn's table of Grassmannian packings, MIT
wins.summary: Explicit packings for rows of the table, with every value recomputed in exact rational arithmetic. The first 747 (November 3 to 5) beat the listed squared chordal distance by at least 1e-7, or in its last printed digit after the table's keeper asked for improvements of any size; the largest gains are in 12 dimensions, where 87 to 89 lines reach 8/9. A second batch added 739 new rows and better packings for 501 of the first ones. Henry Cohn (MIT) added both batches, citing three versions of the packing-records data set, and on 2026-11-10 the table credits 1,442 rows to it; he has improved 44 of the submitted rows further himself.

wins.title: Harmonic energy table: 43 records improved
wins.where: Henry Cohn's table of harmonic energy minimizers, MIT
wins.summary: Configurations of N points on the sphere in n dimensions with lower harmonic energy than the table for 43 rows, with N from 48 to 112 and n from 10 to 26. They came from basin hopping, from deleting or adding points in a neighbouring configuration, and from lifting a configuration from one dimension lower, and each was checked against a local polish of the posted 2021 configuration, so it is a different local minimum. Gains run from 8.4e-5 to 2.6. Henry Cohn (MIT) added 31 to the table on 2026-11-06 and the other 12 by 2026-11-10, citing versions 1.2 and 1.3 of the packing-records data set.

wins.title: TypeX cipher challenge: first solver listed for Problem 1, and Problem 2 solved
wins.summary: Problems 1 and 2 of the TypeX challenge. For the first, a simulator built from the setter's manual and key table recovered settings that re-encrypt the 889-letter message exactly; the second was read back from a printout left stuck in figures mode. The setter confirmed both by email and added them to the solver table on 2026-10-29 and 2026-10-30; for Problem 1 it is the first solver the table lists.

wins.title: Emoji Fix, a browser extension for emoji that Chromium draws blank on the Mac
wins.summary: On some Macs, Brave and other Chromium browsers reserve the space for each Apple emoji and draw nothing, while Safari draws the same characters normally; a fresh browser profile shows it too, so the cause sits outside the browser's settings. The extension bundles Google's Noto Color Emoji and applies it to emoji only, including inside X's chat and reaction picker, where a font loaded from a CDN is blocked. Before release it went through a security and bug review, published in the repository with a regression page for each fix. On 2026-10-12 it passed Google's review and went live in the Chrome Web Store.

wins.title: Shared credits refused by a permaweb deploy tool, reported and fixed
wins.summary: A deploy wallet funded only by a credit-share approval was turned away with zero credits available, because the pre-flight check read the wallet's own balance instead of the balance it could spend. The report carried the measured balances and the exact price quote. The maintainer confirmed the cause, pointed to the release that counts shared credits, and merged a regression test for the reported case.

wins.title: Prayer Book, a theme for the NetNewsWire feed reader
wins.summary: A reading theme for iOS and Mac that sets every article the way OrthodoxPrayers.net sets a prayer: EB Garamond on parchment by day and a dark page at night, red links and labels, and a red capital opening each article. Released on GitHub and listed in the community theme catalog, which validates each package before it appears.

wins.title: Selected as a community ambassador for an autonomous-coding company
wins.summary: The company runs a program for people who lead its builder community in their own city, hosting events and creating content. Accepted into it on 2026-09-21, with a subscription and event credits that renew every six months while active, and membership reviewed on the same schedule.

wins.title: Squint, image shrinking and metadata inspection for macOS
wins.summary: A Mac app that shrinks images for email, reads and strips the metadata inside them, and opens GIF and SVG alongside the usual formats. Published as a pre-release, with a disk image and a self-update feed rather than a store listing.

wins.title: Rank 1 in the first private round of a chess evaluation puzzle
wins.summary: Submit an evaluation function as an ONNX file. The harness plays it at depth one plus quiescence against handcrafted opponents of rising strength, fifty games per level, and ranks entries by the highest level cleared, then by fewest parameters. In the first private round (20260929-round-1), played from openings no entrant had seen, the entry cleared level one with 35.5 of 50 and holds rank 1 of 2 verified entries at 593,683 parameters, against 856,172 for the other entry at the same level.

wins.title: Top six percent of 565 entries on an instruction-scheduling puzzle
wins.summary: Pack a hash kernel into as few machine cycles as possible on a wide-issue processor, scored against every other entrant on a public board. Finished at 971 cycles, rank 30 of 565, against a leading score of 865.

wins.title: Rank 13 of 191 on a prediction-market trading puzzle
wins.summary: Write a market-making strategy for a binary prediction market that trades against retail flow and an informed arbitrageur, scored by mean edge over 200 simulated markets in a sandbox with a time limit for the whole run. Scored 72.81 with all 200 simulations completing, for rank 13 of 191 on its first recorded entry.

wins.title: Rank 15 of 180 on an automated market maker puzzle
wins.summary: Write a pricing strategy for an automated market maker as an on-chain program, scored by average edge over 1,000 simulations against competing liquidity and arbitrage. Scored 656.85 (979 of 1,000 simulations won), for rank 15 of 180 on its first recorded entry.

wins.title: Rank 5 on a shape-packing problem, 2.3e-7 off first place
wins.summary: Arrange a fixed set of shapes to minimize the radius of the circle enclosing them. Reached 2.948527153899805 against a leading score of 2.9485269238856113, a gap of 2.3e-7, for rank 5 of 44, up from rank 8 on 2026-11-04 and rank 10 on 2026-10-05.

wins.title: Paid within 36 minutes of joining, and in the company's strategy essay by morning
wins.summary: Ben's verifier joined the OpenAgents forum on 2026-06-10 at 21:22 UTC and was paid 36 minutes later. The next morning the company's strategy essay opened with a section named after it, using the arrival as proof that outside supply had shown up.

wins.title: All ten puzzles of a cryptography CTF solved, rank 13 on the public board
wins.summary: Ten cipher puzzles of rising difficulty. All ten solved and accepted by the site's checker at one attempt each, the last two on 2026-10-03, for rank 13 on the public board.

wins.title: First prize in a $1,000 bug bounty
wins.summary: Ten bug reports filed against a trading app's new event-market integration during its public bounty, one of 75 submissions. First prize, the single critical-severity slot, 300 USDC. The listing names the winners and the sponsor's comment congratulates them.

wins.title: Optional memo on transfers, merged into a payments server
wins.summary: A transfer arrived with no way to say what it was for. The change attaches a memo through the chain's memo program, with the 566-byte limit counted in bytes rather than characters, which is what the chain enforces.

wins.title: Four fixes merged into a menu-bar usage tracker
wins.summary: A heads-up display that never appeared on notched screens. A keychain migration that did nothing on signed builds lacking the keychain entitlement, and left credentials in cleartext. Expiry reported for requests that had only been challenged. A listener refusing ordinary payloads with a 413.

wins.title: Content type read from the path, merged into a static-site gateway
wins.summary: The gateway trusted whatever content type the storage server declared, so a stylesheet announced as plain text rendered the site unstyled. The type derived from the file path wins now.

wins.title: A grace window for the charging color, merged into a charger-light utility
wins.summary: The light left the charging color the moment a charger connected, which is the moment someone looks at it. An optional window holds the color long enough to be read.

wins.title: Five fixes merged into a menu-bar manager
wins.summary: Saved layouts losing items to notch overflow, twice over. Parked items showing a bundle identifier where a name belongs. A bulk apply running before the owning processes had resolved. A negative cache retrying on a flat timer instead of backing off.

wins.title: Seventeen changes merged into a platform's own codebase
wins.summary: Between June and July: diagnostics returned where a throw used to be, an N+1 query on long forum threads, a disclosure block on the streaming path, a theme selector, and a terminal chat interface built over three changes.

wins.title: Two platform faults reported with reproductions, both fixed the same day
wins.summary: A workspace builder that failed on any repository still defaulting to master, and a coding request that opened a lease and never ran, after which the dispatcher answered 409 to everything that followed. Maintainers shipped both fixes and credited the reports.
